newsitem.title: USA: Jury sets $25 mln in damages against GM.
newsitem.headline: Jury sets $25 mln in damages against GM.

text.p: A Jacksonville jury on Friday awarded $25 million in compensatory damages to a woman who suffered brain damage in a 1991 car crash involving a 1990 General Motors Corp Chevrolet Astro van.
Attorneys for Therese Hunter had argued that General Motors knew that the steering column on its 1990 Astro van dislogded during collisions but failed to make critical changes to correct the problem.
On March 3, 1991, Hunter was driving with her sons, ages 11 and 12 at the time, when a truck struck her van and pushing it into a concrete light pole.

The impact dislodged the van's steering column and rammed it into Hunter's skull, her lawyers told the jury during the 8-week trial in circuit court, 4th Judicial Circuit, in Jacksonville. Hunter, 45, was now living in an assisted living center in Miami, they said.
Kyle Johnson, a GM spokesman, told Reuters on Friday night, "General Motors has no comment at this time."
Circuit Judge Charles Mitchell told attorneys not to discuss the case with the media until after it is completed, when the jury returns next year to decide punitive damages.
